title: Residence Card: What You Must Report, and by When
summary: Four separate notifications, all on a 14 day clock, all free. Missing them is a factor at renewal — and one of the photo rules changed in June 2026.
body_html:
The residence card comes with obligations that are easy to meet and easy to forget, and they share one feature: they all run on 14 days. [source:1] [source:2] [source:3]

Forgetting them is not a fine. It is worse in a quieter way — meeting the notification obligations under the Immigration Act is one of the things the agency weighs when you renew. [source:4]

Your address, when you first settle

Once you have decided where you live, report that address at the municipal office for the area, in person, bringing your residence card. [source:1] The deadline is 14 days from deciding the address. [source:1]

If your passport carries the note saying the card will be issued later, bring the passport instead. [source:1] On that route the card is issued after this report and posted to the address you registered. [source:1]

One saving: this report can be filed together with the resident registration move-in notification at the same window. [source:1] Ask for both.

Your address, when you move

If you change address, report the new one within 14 days of moving in, again bringing your residence card to the municipal office for the new area. [source:1]

This is the one students miss most often, because moving flat does not feel like an immigration event. It is. And unreported addresses are a cancellation ground in their own right.

Your school, when anything changes about it

If your institution changes its name or address, ceases to exist, or if you leave it or transfer to another, you must notify the Commissioner of the Immigration Services Agency within 14 days. [source:2]

This one goes to immigration, not the municipal office, and it is the easiest of the four to file.

You can use the electronic notification system, available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, which also shows your filing history and processing status. [source:2] Or go to a regional immigration office with your residence card. [source:2] Or post the form with a copy of your card. [source:2]

No documents evidencing the notified matter are required. [source:2] There is nothing to assemble.

If you post it, the agency sends no acknowledgement of receipt and recommends a trackable method. [source:2] Use the online system.

A lost card: 14 days, and the clock starts when you notice [source:3]

If you lose possession of your card through loss, theft, destruction or other cause, you apply for reissue under Article 19-12. [source:3]

The deadline is 14 days from the day you learned of the fact — or, if you learned of it while outside Japan, from the day you first entered afterwards. [source:3] That second clause is more generous than people assume: losing your card on holiday abroad does not put you in breach while you are still away.

What the application needs:

  • No fee. [source:3]
  • One photograph meeting the specified format. [source:3]
  • For loss or theft, a written statement about it — and you need a police report acceptance number, so report it to the police first. [source:3]

Processing is same-day issuance as a rule. [source:3] There is no appeal procedure. [source:3]

And if you are past the 14 days, that is not the end: a document stating the reasons is additionally required. [source:3] Late is a form to fill in. Never filing is a different problem.

The photo rule changed in June 2026 [source:3]

This one is recent enough that older guides are wrong about it.

No photograph is required for a person under 1 year of age on the date the card is issued. [source:3] The agency notes the change explicitly: before 13 June 2026 the photo exemption applied to those under 16 years of age, and for cards issued from 14 June 2026 a photograph is required for people aged 1 and over. [source:3]

So if you are a student with a child in Japan, or you are reading advice written before that date, the age threshold you remember is no longer the one in force.

Separately, for a lost-card application the applicant is the person themselves, excluding those under 16 years of age, with defined proxies available otherwise. [source:3]

Why these add up

The renewal guideline lists meeting the Immigration Act's notification obligations among its considerations, and names them: notifications relating to the entries on your residence card, applications to renew the card's validity, applications to reissue a lost card, returning the card, and notifications concerning your affiliated institution. [source:4] It cites Articles 19-7 to 19-13, Article 19-15 and Article 19-16. [source:4]

Every item on this page is in that list. None of them costs money. Two of them can be done online or in one visit to a counter you are already going to.

That is an unusually good deal: a set of obligations where compliance is nearly free and non-compliance sits in your file.

The four clocks, together

  • First address: 14 days from deciding it. [source:1] Municipal office, in person, card in hand. [source:1]
  • Change of address: 14 days from moving in. [source:1] New municipal office. [source:1]
  • School changes, you leave or transfer: 14 days. [source:2] Immigration, online is easiest, no supporting documents. [source:2]
  • Lost card: 14 days from when you learned of it. [source:3] Police report first, then immigration. [source:3]

If you are leaving or changing school, the notification is only part of it — see what happens to your status if you stop attending or withdraw. For the full renewal picture, including the tax and insurance items that catch people quietly, see what immigration actually looks at when you renew. For the arrival sequence these obligations start from, see your first week in Japan.

Procedures and forms change — the photo rule above changed in 2026 [source:3] — and the agency's pages linked below are the authority. This page is a summary, not advice.

claims_without_sources: 届出を怠った場合の罰則の条文・内容 —— 各手続ページに罰則の記載がなく、入管法の条文を直接確認していないため書いていない。更新ガイドラインが届出義務の履行を考慮要素に挙げている点のみ出典付きで述べた。
汚損・毀損による再交付（紛失とは別手続）—— 別ページの管轄で、本記事では確認していないため触れていない。
在留カードの有効期間更新申請の期限 —— ガイドラインが義務として列挙しているが、期限は別ページにあり確認していないため、期限を書いていない。
住居地届出を14日以内に行わなかった場合の実務的な扱い —— 取消事由としての90日は別記事で扱ったが、14日超過時の窓口での扱いは公表されていない。紛失再交付のみ「超過時は理由書が別途必要」と出典に明記があるため書いた。
警察への遺失届の出し方・必要なもの —— 警察の管轄であり入管庁の出典にはない。「先に警察へ届け出て受理番号が必要」という出典の記述までに留めた。
